newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Council strongly deplores Sierra Leone coup.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Council strongly deplores Sierra Leone coup.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council late on Tuesday strongly deplored the military coup in Sierra Leone and called for an immediate restoration of what it termed constitutional order.
In a tough statement read at a formal meeting, the council also condemned violence against both the local and foreign communities, particularly United Nations personnel in the country.
The 15-member council said "it strongly deplores this attempt to overthrow the democratically elected government and called for an immediate restoration of constitutional order."

The statement, initiated by Britain, also recalled the "obligations of all concerned to ensure the protection of the United Nations and other international personnel in the country and calls for an end to the looting of premises and equipment belonging to the United Nations and international aid agencies."
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Sunday said he was "distressed" about the coup and condemned the damage to U.N. headquarters and some local staff taken into custody.
The coup leaders, which Sierra Leone's U.N. ambassador James Jonah said included a group of dissatisfied corporals, this weekend overthrew the elected government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
He has fled to Guinea and asked West African countries, whose military arm is led by Nigeria, to help restore his government, Jonah said.
